bib.title: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning" (ReHarness), Yuxin Xiao (MIT; work done during internship at Meta MRS Research), Zhiyun Lu, Jianyu Wang, Yang Song, Qifan Wang, Bailin Wang (Meta MRS Research), Yangtian Zhang (Yale). arXiv 2610.12668v1 [cs.LG], preprint, dated 12 Oct 2026 on the page (arXiv stamp 8 Oct 2026).
COVERAGE: All 20 of 20 pages read, 72,585 chars. Main text pp.1-10, references pp.11-14, appendix pp.15-20 (Tables 5-7, prompts, two worked examples). The appendix tables were read; the prompt and example text on pp.18-20 was only skimmed. No embedded instructions found. Extraction was clean.

MAIN CLAIM: Stored reflections are usually written once and never corrected. ReHarness adds a backward revision step. After each instance, a revision agent rewrites the reflections retrieved for that instance, using the new trajectory as feedback. Any new content must stay grounded in the reflection's own source trajectory. This corrects overgeneralised or outdated lessons under a strict online stream, with no replay, no validation set and no gradient updates.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. Average normalized gain 0.240 for ReHarness. Setup: 3 benchmarks (CL-Bench, MemoryBench, MemoryArena), 3 backbones (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.7 Flash), 3 stream rollouts, top-k=5. Baselines: Full Raw 0.164, Top-K Raw 0.168, GEPA-Online 0.092, Mem0 0.131, ACE 0.043, DoT 0.071, RBank 0.034 (Table 1). Normalized gain is (r_method - r_stateless)/(r_max - r_stateless). Significance: paired Wilcoxon with Bonferroni, p_adj < 0.05 against all baselines; Top-K Raw p_adj = 0.039, Full Raw p_adj = 0.043. The unit is a seeded task stream.
2. Ablation, CL-Bench with Claude (Table 3): no revision 0.144, ReHarness 0.217, counterfactual replay (revised harness applied to the same instance, which breaks the streaming protocol) 0.335. Removing the revised reflections used as demonstrations in the write step drops 0.217 to 0.191.
3. Stability and plasticity on CL-Bench (Table 4): Mem0, RBank, DoT, ACE and GEPA-Online have negative average stability gains. ReHarness averages +0.015 stability and 0.241 plasticity.
4. Cost, one CL-Bench rollout with Claude: ReHarness ~41.57M tokens (~$254), Top-K Raw ~52.66M (~$85), Full Raw ~142.12M (~$314).
Also: over 95% of revised claims stay source-grounded, with leakage 0.8-2.1% (Table 2, CL-Bench, GPT-5.6-Sol as claim judge).

QUOTES
- p.4: "Misleading reflections can persist in the harness state and propagate errors through later retrievals."
- p.1: "once written, memories and reflections are rarely updated based on their effectiveness on later instances."
- p.8 (database example): after a schema shift added "prc_v2", the stale reflection "the graded value came from prc" was revised to "enumerate all price-like columns".

LIMITS
- The authors concede two limits (p.10). Exploitable poker is a weak spot, because noisy rewards give poor revision signal. ReHarness also keeps raw trajectories for future revision, so it has a storage overhead.
- The paper also says ReHarness "benefits most when feedback is diagnostic". It relies on a reward signal. Whether it works without one is not shown.
- Gains against raw-context baselines are modest and the p-values are borderline (0.039 and 0.043). Full Raw ties or beats ReHarness in some cells (Table 1: GPT on MemoryArena 0.358 vs 0.358, Gemini CL-Bench 0.234 vs 0.233).
- It revises only the k=5 retrieved reflections, and gain declines for larger k, which the authors attribute to "reflection drift". The k sweep was run on one benchmark with one model (CL-Bench, Claude) and is described as post-hoc.
- The grounding check uses an LLM judge, not human audit.
- Streams are short (12 to 270 instances per task), and the baselines are re-implemented adaptations (GEPA-Online is the authors' own adaptation).
- It does not show long-lived production memory, memory poisoning, contradictions between users, or deletion and forgetting policies.
- Some model and judge names in the paper may not match what you expect (Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6-Sol). I report them as printed.

BUILDS ON: Mem0 (Chhikara et al., ECAI 2025); Reflection Bank (Ouyang et al., 2026); Diversity of Thought (Lingam et al., 2025); ACE, Agentic Context Engineering (Zhang et al., ICLR 2026); GEPA (Agrawal et al., ICLR 2026); ExpeL (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024); Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) and TextGrad (Yuksekgonul et al., 2024) for textual feedback; claim decomposition from Min et al. (2023); benchmarks CL-Bench (Asawa et al., 2026), MemoryBench (Ai et al., ICML 2026), MemoryArena (He et al., 2026).

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 1, p.3. It uses a sort-ascending/descending example. The forward-only harness keeps retrieving the overgeneralised "put larger numbers first", while ReHarness revises it to "larger first only if descending". It shows the memory-correction idea faster than prose. Alternative: Figure 3, p.9, the blind spectrum and prc_v2 schema-shift revisions.
